history.period: Tradition claims over 1,000 years (11th century); no authenticated founding inscription; renovated 2009
history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the temple is in YELLUR village, not Udupi town (Udupi is the district). This is a Swayambhu (self-manifested) Shiva linga temple, said to be over 1,000 years old and referred to in 12 rock edicts; Vadiraja Tirtha extols Vishweshwara here in five slokas of the Tirtha Prabandha. Legends: (1) Lord Ullaya, pleased with the penance of a Kunda Hegde devotee, descended from Kashi to Yelluru; (2) the linga emerged from underground for a Samanta Raja of the Kuthyar dynasty, and was found by a Koraga woman who struck a tuber while searching for her dead son Yellu - the 'bleeding' earth proved to be the linga, whose wound-mark is still shown, and the village took the name Yellur; devotees pour tender coconut water and offer coconut oil as expiation. The temple is a noted Devaayathana-style model. It was renovated from scratch and re-inaugurated 4-12 March 2009. Coordinates are the temple coordinates published on Wikipedia (infobox), not independently verified on the ground.

name: Shri Vishweshwara Temple, Yellur
town_description: Yellur is a village in Udupi district, Karnataka, on the coastal plain between Udupi and Mangaluru. It is a Tulu-speaking agricultural village with lush vegetation and fertile fields; the Udupi Power Plant was set up in and around Yellur. The Mahathobhara Vishweshwara Temple stands at the village boundary and serves as the worship epicentre for Yellur and the neighbouring Maagane villages (Belapu, Kunjoor, Kuthyar, Padoor and others).
